title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Printing and Issuing the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the System for Presidents, Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, and Deputy Division Chiefs to Participate in Collegial Panels for Trial of Cases
keywords_en: Deputy chief judge participating in collegial panel hearing of a case
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the System for Presidents, Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, and Deputy Division Chiefs to Participate in Collegial Panels for Trial Work

Fa Fa [2007] No. 14

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the System for Presidents, Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, and Deputy Division Chiefs to Participate in Collegial Panels for Trial Work were adopted at the 1416th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby issued to you for your compliance and implementation in light of the actual circumstances of trial work.

March 30, 2007

Supreme People's Court

Several Opinions on Improving the System for Presidents, Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, and Deputy Division Chiefs to Participate in Collegial Panels for Trial Work

To enable the presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs of the People's Courts to better perform their trial duties, these Opinions are formulated in light of the actual circumstances of trial work.

Article 1. Presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs of People's Courts at all levels shall, in addition to participating in the trial of cases through the Judicial Committee, participate in collegial panels or serve as sole judges to try cases each year.

Article 2. Presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs shall participate in collegial panels to try the following categories of cases:

(1) Difficult, complex, and major cases;

(2) New types of cases;

(3) Cases that have general significance in the application of law; and

(4) Cases that they consider should be tried by a collegial panel in which they participate.

Article 3. The quantitative standards for cases handled by the President, Vice-Presidents, Division Chiefs, and Deputy Division Chiefs of the Supreme People's Court shall be prescribed by the Supreme People's Court.

The quantitative standards for cases handled by the presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs of local People's Courts at all levels shall be prescribed by the People's Court at the corresponding level in accordance with the actual local circumstances. The quantitative standards for case handling prescribed by Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts shall be reported to the Higher People's Court for record.

Presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs shall select a certain number of cases and personally assume the role of the responsible judge to handle them.

Article 4. When handling cases, presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs shall serve as role models. At the same time, they shall pay attention to summarizing trial work experience and standardizing and guiding trial work.

Article 5. When presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs participate in collegial panels to try cases, they shall, in accordance with the law, serve as the presiding judge and shall enjoy equal voting rights with other members of the collegial panel.

When presidents or vice-presidents participate in the deliberation of a collegial panel and the majority opinion is inconsistent with the opinion of the president or vice-president, the president or vice-president may decide to submit the case to the Judicial Committee for discussion. Among the members of the collegial panel, those who are not members of the Judicial Committee shall attend the Judicial Committee meeting as non-voting participants.

Article 6. Once the trial date is set for a case handled by a president, vice-president, division chief, or deputy division chief, it shall not be changed arbitrarily.

Article 7. The participation of presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs in collegial panels to try cases shall be regarded as an important task in the performance of their trial duties and shall be included in the scope of assessment and supervision of their work.

Article 8. These Opinions shall come into effect as of the date of issuance.
